signOffConditionVerdicts.note: Every item is vehicle-reported, and the evidence is the inbound message rather than the item's name: each of the five is populated by a NAMED_VALUE_INT or NAMED_VALUE_FLOAT arriving from the aircraft, which the accepted DG-TLM:dialect record settles as the Aerora reporting mechanism. sprayPumpCommand is the one that reads like a counter-example and is not: the name describes what the value is, the pump command the flight controller computed, and the station only ever receives it. No item here is a station-originated request, a parameter write or a station-derived projection, so criterion 7 does not engage and the guard verdicts below keep the outbound direction shut. The two gimbal items the firmware model carries are deliberately not in the set: the accepted dialect record declares no gimbal fact, a gimbal is a camera concern upstream already models, and whether it is Aerora content at all is an open Product question rather than something this signature answers.

guardPermissions.reason: Settling which values the aircraft reports settles the inbound direction and nothing else. Knowing that sprayEnabled and sprayPumpCommand arrive as NAMED_VALUE_* does not permit the station to drive the applicator, which stays the payload controller's concern. The same verdict DG-ROL:authorization-scope reached on this guard, for the same reason read from the other side.

Nothing in a reported item set permits the station to originate a payload action without an operator asking for one. P7-PAY-004's reported-values-only rule is recorded as excluded from this Gate precisely because it is not what a signature here decides.

entries.value: Settled as a reported item with an unsettled enumeration, on the terms the accepted DG-TLM:dialect record already set for this same item against an identically worded criterion. Four of the five attributes are known: the item name is sprayGateState, it carries no unit because it is an enumeration, its value range is the int32 range NAMED_VALUE_INT carries, and its reporting message is NAMED_VALUE_INT. Only the member set is unsettled, because the interlock is a Stateflow chart and the firmware archive does not enumerate its states. Recorded as an explicit exception rather than guessed: with NAMED_VALUE_INT the integer is what travels, so a guessed member becomes permanent in every flight log the first time firmware sends it. Appending members later is safe; renumbering silently rewrites records already on disk. The station displays the reported integer and interprets none of it until the members are settled by amendment.
